title: Compatibility sunset playbook for deprecated request headers and client-side adapter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD-style playbook to retire a set of legacy request headers and parameter encodings that client SDKs and third-party integrators still use. This ticket defines the migration path, acceptance criteria, telemetry gates, rollout windows, rollback conditions, and client-side adapter specifications required to minimize customer disruption.
background: Over time several request headers (X-legacy-session, X-compat-params) and a binary legacy parameter encoding were introduced to support early performance experiments. These are now blocking simplifications in the unified inference API and make routing/observability more complex. Prior deprecation notes were not prescriptive enough for SDKs and platform partners; this playbook provides an operational migration path and explicit safety gates.
scope_included:
- Identify exact set of headers and encodings to remove (primary list below)
- Provide SDK adapter specs and reference implementation (JS + Python)
- Define telemetry and opt-in shadowing mode for 8-week migration
- Communication plan: devblog, changelog, in-Console migration banner, and direct emails to active integrators
- Create rollout schedule with gradual regional removal and traffic-based gating
- Acceptance criteria and automated test matrix for regressions
scope_excluded:
- Changes to model aliasing or model sunset timelines (handled separately)
- Internal runtime kernel changes unrelated to header parsing
- Billing/usage pricing changes
legacy_items_list:
- X-legacy-session (session affinity header)
- X-compat-params (legacy param bundle)
- legacy-param-encoding=v1 (binary proto form)
- X-client-feature-flags (deprecated ternary encoding)
acceptance_criteria: All production traffic for 95% of customers flows successfully when adapters translate deprecated headers to canonical headers in shadow and live modes
No increase in 99th percentile latency for unified/generate endpoints above 5% compared to baseline after adapter rollout
Automated compatibility test suite (JS+Py) passes against prod-mock and dedicated canary cluster
Telemetry gates report <1% error spike and client-side migration progress shows >65% adoption in target cohort before hard removal
Support runbook and SDK migration guide published and reviewed by Developer Experience and Support leads
migration_steps: 1) Triage & finalize legacy item list with Engineering and Security (2 weeks)
2) Implement server-side compatibility adapter that accepts legacy headers and emits canonical headers; run in shadow mode only (4 weeks)
3) Publish SDK adapter pattern and reference implementations; enable opt-in client-side translation flag (2 weeks)
4) Open beta: enable shadow translation in Console for targeted orgs; collect telemetry and support feedback (4 weeks)
5) Graduated rollout: region-by-region opt-out window with daily telemetry review and a 72-hour hold window for anomalies (6 weeks)
6) Hard removal: disable server acceptance of deprecated headers after 8 weeks of gated stability for primary cohort (1 day)
telemetry_gates: Adoption metric: percent of requests without deprecated headers (goal > 65% in cohort)
Error budget: 24h rolling increase in 5xxs attributable to header parsing < 0.5% of baseline errors
Latency budget: P99 increase attributable to adapter work < 5%
Support noise: number of migration-related support tickets per day < 1% of pre-rollout volume
Security signals: no new alerts raised by static/dynamic analysis tied to adapter
rollback_criteria: Sustained P99 latency > threshold for 3 consecutive days in the region under rollout
Error rate attribution shows >1% of requests failing due to header translation path
Significant customer-reported functional regressions affecting >3 strategic customers
Any critical security finding in the adapter within the 72-hour hold window
dependencies: ENG-20577 (compat test harness and canary infra)
PM-271110 (customer communications calendar and legal review)
release_notes_summary: Deprecation: Removal of legacy request headers and legacy binary parameter encoding. We provide adapters and SDK guides to minimize disruption. Hard removal scheduled after migration window and telemetry gates met.
